newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean president's son faces arrest for bribery.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean president's son faces arrest for bribery.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors sought an arrest warrant on Saturday for President Kim Young-sam's son on charges of bribery and tax evasion, a prosecution official said.
The official said prosecutors were seeking to arrest Kim Hyun-chul for accepting kickbacks worth 3.2 billion won ($3.6 million) in return for favours.
He has denied accepting bribes.
Kim Hyun-chul would also be charged with evading taxes on 3.3 billion won given to him by businessmen, but not as bribes.
A request for the arrest of the younger Kim, dubbed the "crown prince", was filed with a Seoul court.

An arrest is widely expected later on Saturday, bringing to a climax a corruption scandal involving top politicians, bankers and businessmen that emerged from the rubble of the country's biggest bankruptcy in January.
If convicted of bribery, Kim Hyun-chul faces a maximum sentence of five years in jail.

Public attention is now riveted on President Kim, who has been badly wounded by the scandal linked to the failure of Hanbo Steel Co. The president is expected to issue an apology next week after his son is arrested and detained.
Kim Hyun-chul was summoned by state prosecutors for questioning on Thursday and has been at the Supreme Public Prosecutors' Office ever since.
Prosecutors have said he admitted taking money from a group of businessmen who were alumni of his high school. But he denied the money represented bribes.
The prosecutors were probing allegations that Kim Hyun-chul used his huge influence to obtain lucrative broadcasting, cable television and telecommunications licences for associates.
In addition, they were looking into allegations that he laundered through companies owned by his cronies as much as 10 billion won of unspent funds from his father's 1992 election campaign.
The election slush funds have become a hot political issue for his father, who is under growing public pressure to make a full accounting of his 1992 campaign finances.

South Korean media reported on Saturday that Kim Hyun-chul had written a letter to a friend before being summoned vowing to "use all means at my disposal to fight any legal prosecution, including arrest".
"I will wage this fight not as the son of the president but as Hyun-chul, an individual," the letter was quoted as saying.
Officials at the presidential Blue House, who are anxious to put the scandal behind them as quickly as possible, were clearly stunned by the report.
"It is a mere expression of an emotional young man's feelings," the Korean Times quoted one unnamed presidential aide as saying.
Opposition parties have alleged that Hanbo Steel received preferential loans as a reward for donations of up to 90 billion won to Kim Young-sam's election campaign.
Eleven people, including three top aides of President Kim, are standing trial over the Hanbo scandal.
Kim Young-sam was swept to power on an anti-graft ticket, and put his two immediate predecessors, Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, into jail on corruption and other charges.
